issues.detail: Both examples are short prose walkthroughs that mostly refer back to earlier snippets instead of showing complete runnable end-to-end code or expected output.

scenarios.name: local-stack-and-v4-signin
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric: it installs `@nhost/cli`, runs `npx nhost init` and `npx nhost up`, uses `createClient` with local subdomain and region, calls `signInEmailPassword`, reads `res.body.session`, and wraps the call in try/catch for the thrown FetchError. A installs the CLI with a curl script and runs bare `nhost init` and `nhost up` instead of `@nhost/cli` with npx. It does use `createClient`, `signInEmailPassword` and try/catch, but its install path misses the rubric's first requirement.

scenarios.name: hasura-posts-permissions-and-paginated-query
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely: correct `_or` select filter, `set` on insert, own-row update filter, `nhost.graphql.request` with limit/offset, order_by and aggregate, and it checks `res.body.errors` and throws. B has the right permissions but uses graphql-request instead of the Nhost SDK, never checks for GraphQL errors, and writes `x-hasura-User-Id` in the insert `set` with the wrong case, so it is less correct there.

scenarios.name: private-pdf-upload-with-expiring-link
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses uploadFiles with bucket-id and file[], takes processedFiles[0], inserts via insert_documents_one, calls getFilePresignedURL and reads res.body.url, says the URL expires, and mentions Hasura rules on storage.files, though only vaguely. A leads with the older v2/v3 API (storage.upload, getPresignedUrl) and puts the rubric's API only in a hedged v4 section that is unverified and doesn't take the id from processedFiles in the main flow, though it does cover expiry and storage.files permissions well.
